item.description:
Sidetone 1.1.1

A fraction of the processor it used to take.

  • Monitoring with the panel closed took about fourteen per cent of a processor core. It now takes about one, which is battery back and a fan that stays quiet.
  • The panel costs less to keep open as well, and the meters move as smoothly as they did.
  • When a device you chose is unplugged, the panel names the device actually in use, rather than one that nothing is coming from.

Sidetone 1.1.0

Tone controls, and pickers that can follow the system default.

  • Bass and treble either side of a low cut, under Settings, Audio. The low cut takes out rumble and fan noise, and you choose where it sits.
  • Presets now carry the tone along with the devices and the gain. Presets saved by 1.0.0 still load.
  • Leave a picker on System default and monitoring follows whatever macOS is using, so putting headphones on moves it to them.
  • Monitoring can start on its own when your devices are plugged in, under Settings, General.
  • The panel closes when you open Settings, and when a display or Space change would otherwise strand it in the middle of the screen.
  • Fixes a start that switched itself off and on again, and one that gave up for good when a device went missing for a moment.

Sidetone 1.0.0

First release.

  • Sends any input to any output, so you can hear your own microphone, or a line-in from something else.
  • Capture and playback run on independent clocks, joined by a ring buffer with drift correction, so mismatched devices keep working.
  • Level meter, spectrum, gain in dB with a click-free ramp, and a safety limiter.
  • Latency profiles that start as tight as your devices allow and back off if your Mac cannot keep up.
  • Global shortcuts, named presets, and devices remembered across unplugging.
  • Stops and starts itself around sleep, and tells you if a device disappears.
